title: Data-driven RNA phenotyping captures genetically regulated dimensions of the transcriptome.

verified.what_i_actually_checked: Listed Zenodo record 19924423 via API (CC-BY-4.0; 15 files; rna_phenotypes.zip 30.4 GB, laddr_models.zip 3.2 GB, qtls.zip 577 MB). Read README.md. Downloaded qtls.gtex-ddp.tsv.gz (28.8 MB): 1,549,097 rows, 6 columns (tissue, gene_id, rank, phenotype_id, variant_id, pval_beta); 49 tissues, 40,941 genes, 254,318 phenotypes like ENSG...__PC6. No effect size, no fine-mapping probability column.
verified.what_came_from_paper_text_only: That LaDDR phenotypes are per-gene PCA (principal component analysis) components of binned RNA-seq coverage; the 95% more xQTLs claim; TWAS (transcriptome-wide association study) counts across 114 traits. Did not open per-tissue cis_qtl files inside qtls.zip, nor the 30 GB phenotype tables. GTEx individual genotypes are dbGaP controlled access (known, not tested).

a1_downloadable.note: Summary results on Zenodo, open, CC-BY-4.0; checked file listing and downloaded one table. Individual-level GTEx genotypes needed for any new QTL mapping are dbGaP controlled access.

a2_label_is_a_column.note: Checked file: only lead variant + p-value per latent phenotype. A causal-variant or effect label would have to be constructed by fine-mapping, which needs controlled-access genotypes or LD (linkage disequilibrium) modelling.

a3_inputs_present.note: Variant IDs encode hg38 coordinates and alleles (chr1_665098_G_A_b38), so sequence can be pulled from the reference genome; checked in file.

a4_units_stated.note: p-values are unitless; README documents phenotype normalization (quantile + inverse-normal).

a5_enough_rows.note: 1,549,097 independent xQTL rows in the aggregated DDP (data-driven phenotype) table, counted in file.

a6_fits_laptop.working_set: ~30-600 MB for QTL tables; 30 GB for phenotype matrices
a6_fits_laptop.note: QTL tables fit; full phenotype matrices do not but are not needed for a QTL-level task.

a7_counts_match_paper.note: Not cross-checked against the paper's per-tissue counts; 49 tissues matches the paper.

a8_label_provenance.note: The phenotype is a PCA axis computed by the LaDDR model per gene, so 'PC6' means something different for every gene; the 'label' is a statistical association to that model output, with lead variants confounded by LD rather than measured causal effects.

existing_models.name: AlphaGenome (DNA sequence model, DeepMind)
existing_models.score_and_split: On fine-mapped GTEx QTLs: AUC (area under the ROC curve) 0.80 for splicing QTLs, 0.86 for polyadenylation QTLs; recovers 41% of GTEx eQTLs at 90% sign accuracy (per search snippet of preprint).

existing_models.name: Borzoi / Enformer (DNA sequence-to-coverage models)
existing_models.score_and_split: Borzoi recovers 19% of GTEx eQTLs at 90% sign accuracy (as reported in AlphaGenome preprint snippet).

backbone.name: AlphaGenome
backbone.hardware: CPU too slow for genome-scale scoring; API or GPU

integration.bigger_question_one_sentence: Do sequence models predict the extra QTLs found only by annotation-free latent phenotypes? — but labels are LD-confounded leads, so the answer would be uninterpretable.

controls.positive_control: Known eQTL lead variants overlapping KDP (knowledge-driven phenotype) xQTLs.
controls.negative_control: Matched non-QTL variants at same distance to TSS.
controls.external_validation: Geuvadis LaDDR xQTLs in the same record.

honest_claim_h3: A model could at best claim to rank which variants are lead associations for arbitrary per-gene latent coverage components in GTEx, not which variants causally alter RNA.

plain_idea.one_liner: Use DNA sequence around a genetic variant to predict whether it is linked to hidden patterns of RNA coverage in human tissues.
plain_idea.train_on: DNA sequence windows around 1,549,097 variant-gene-tissue lead associations (verified count) plus matched non-associated variants.
plain_idea.predict: Whether a variant is the lead association for a data-driven RNA phenotype; the truth comes from statistical association testing on GTEx RNA-seq and genotypes, not a direct measurement.
plain_idea.why_worthwhile: Would tell regulatory geneticists whether sequence models capture the regulation missed by annotated modalities, but lead-variant labels are confounded by correlated nearby variants.

more_or_better_data.why: LaDDR adds about 95% more xQTLs per tissue than the six annotated modalities, but these are on the same GTEx v8 individuals AlphaGenome and Borzoi were already benchmarked on.

confidence_score.why: Aggregated table has only a p-value per lead variant; no replicate or fine-mapping probabilities to calibrate against.

models_beatable.why: AlphaGenome (2025-2026, large pretrained transformer) is evaluated on fine-mapped GTEx QTLs with AUC 0.80-0.86.

guaranteed_improvement.why: The new labels measure a different, model-defined quantity (latent PCs), not the same quantity the baseline was evaluated on.

ml_idea: Considered: sequence model (AlphaGenome embeddings + head) to classify LaDDR-specific xQTL lead variants vs matched controls, transferring to Geuvadis. Rejected because labels are LD-confounded associations to model-defined latent axes.

effort.compute_note: Not estimated; scoring ~1.5M variants with a DNA foundation model is GPU/API scale.
effort.cheapest_killing_check: Check whether any per-tissue file has fine-mapping posterior probabilities (none in the aggregated table).

verdict_reason: A2 and A8 fail: the only labels are lead-variant p-values for per-gene PCA components produced by the LaDDR model itself, so the label is a model output with no consistent meaning across genes, and LD confounds which variant is causal. Fine-mapping to build a real label needs dbGaP genotypes, and AlphaGenome already covers GTEx QTL prediction.
